text:
kai (customer): Hey team — our app's streaming websocket to our Private/VPC Redwood deployment (vpc-prod.redwood.example) goes silent after ~25-35s, then eventually resets. Only happens from our prod VPC behind a corporate firewall/egress allowlist. Hosted Redwood endpoints are fine. This started after we changed the firewall last Friday.

kai (customer): Minimal repro: connect with wscat and no traffic, after ~30s connection stops receiving chunks. No obvious errors in app logs.

jordan (support): Sorry you're hitting this — thanks for the repro. Can you paste the exact wscat/curl you used and a tcpdump/pcap around the failure? Also confirm whether you use any ingress proxy (NGINX/Haproxy) in front of the Redwoods endpoint in the VPC.

kai (customer): Using wscat: `wscat -c \"wss://vpc-prod.redwood.internal/stream?token=REDACTED\"`
Result: connects, then after ~30s client sees silence, eventually: "WebSocket connection closed" with code 1006. Server logs show the stream still running for a bit, then reports write error.

kai (customer): I ran a short tcpdump on the client side (filtered to port 443). Excerpt:
```
13:02:05.123 IP client > redwood  TLSv1.3  Application Data
13:02:20.456 IP client > redwood  TLSv1.3  Application Data
13:02:35.789 IP client > redwood  TLSv1.3  Application Data
13:02:36.001 IP redwood > client  [RST]
```
No FIN prior to RST.

jordan (support): That looks like an abrupt close from the peer (RST). Two likely culprits given "private VPC + firewall change": a stateful firewall/NAT dropping idle connections after ~30s, or a middlebox that buffers and then injects RST. Can you check your firewall/NAT idle timeout? Many appliances default to ~30s for TCP state. Also does your egress allowlist proxy do TLS interception / MITM? If so, TLS renegotiation or ALPN mismatches can trigger midbox resets.

sara (eng-runtime): Quick checklist from runtime side:
- Verify TLS SNI/ALPN are preserved end-to-end. Run: `openssl s_client -connect vpc-prod.redwood.internal:443 -servername vpc-prod.redwood.internal -alpn h2` and confirm certificate chain and ALPN.
- If you have an HTTP proxy/NGINX in path, ensure websocket passthrough without buffering (nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 360s; proxy_send_timeout 360s;`).
- If traffic is NAT'd, ensure TCP keepalives or websocket pings are configured on the client side.

sara (eng-runtime): Nginx example snippet to avoid buffering for websockets:
```
location /stream/ {
  proxy_pass https://redwood-upstream;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
  proxy_set_header Connection $http_connection;
  proxy_read_timeout 600s;
}
```

jordan (support): Also check if your firewall/egress allowlist permits our streaming cluster IP ranges and doesn't terminate idle TCP state too aggressively. If you can't change the firewall settings quickly, a pragmatic workaround is to enable periodic websocket pings (client->server) every 15-20s so the connection stays active.

kai (customer): Ran `openssl s_client` as suggested — cert chain verified (verify return:1), ALPN offered: h2,http/1.1. No MITM certificate seen. So likely not TLS interception.

kai (customer): We scanned firewall logs. It shows a connection-state expiration rule firing ~30s after last observed client data: `state: TCP_IDLE_TIMEOUT_EXPIRED src=client dst=redwood`

jordan (support): That confirms it. The firewall is timing out idle TCP flows and sending RST. Two options: increase the TCP idle timeout for long-lived streaming flows, or ensure periodic keepalive/heartbeat frames.

sara (eng-runtime): Additional note for customers running gateways that buffer: if you see buffered data delivered in a burst right before the RST, that's the middlebox holding the TLS records. We recommend combining server-side small-chunk flushes + client pings. Server can emit a 1 byte chunk (or ping) every 20s when idle. Also double-check any TCP MSS/clamp settings on the NAT that might cause unexpected fragmentation.

jordan (support): For repro/data, it helps to capture a short pcap on both sides (client and upstream) showing the silence then RST. If you can attach a 30s pcap to the ticket we can escalate to network infra.

kai (customer): We patched quickly: increased firewall idle timeout to 10m and enabled client websocket ping every 15s (we already had server pings, but client didn't). After change: no more mid-30s resets. Streams stay healthy.

jordan (support): Awesome — glad that fixed it. We'll add a short KB note recommending websocket heartbeats and a checklist for VPC/firewall settings (idle timeout > 5m, allowlist Redwood streaming IP ranges).

kai (customer): Thanks all — appreciate the help. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: Ticket #12345 updated with notes: "root cause: stateful firewall idle timeout; mitigation: increase idle timeout and enable client heartbeat"

sara (eng-runtime): Follow-up: we'll add a small blurb to our Private deployment docs reminding customers to tune firewall/NAT timeouts and consider short default client heartbeat guidance (15s) for websocket streaming workloads.
